text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- GDP growth remains sluggish with an 0.2 percent rise in the first quarter of 1997.
-- Labour minister Martine Aubry calls for an organised and controlled economic pickup.
-- Blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 2.11 percent Thursday, as investors expect a continuity of economic policy.
-- Pernod-Ricard set to buying spirits unit from Spanish group Larios for 1.4 billion francs, and doubling its Spanish activity.
-- Lagardere seeks to increase activity in the United States, notably in multimedia.
-- BNP and Credit Lyonnais are insured against possible legal action against them linked to the management of Eurotunnel funding.
-- Shoemaker Groupe Andre to implement restructuring plan including some 400 job cuts and shut-down of 81 shops.
-- Paris stock exchange hails the new government, remains unaffected by slow GDP growth reported for Q1 1997.
Due to a strike the newspaper is not published today.

-- CFDT union head Nicole Notat says in an interview she is sceptical about a shift to a 35-hour work week without wage cuts, called for by the Socialists. She adds privatisations can be key to industrial alliances.
-- French investors see room for hope. Shares rise on signs that Socialists support the euro.
